parsed.reason: The facts check out against the notes: NIH short-term safety, UC Davis's one-to-two-month window, the preliminary November 2025 AHA abstract (no proof of cause, possible poor-sleep confound) and the dose disagreement. 'It hasn't been peer-reviewed' is a slight present-tense stretch, since the notes don't say whether the study was published later, but it matches the AHA framing. It gives no dosing regimen and makes no diagnosis. The doctor or pharmacist pointer and the nudge to look at what's behind ongoing sleep trouble are the right care. It loses a point on tone: it is source-heavy and long, closer to a research summary than a casual text, though it still answers directly.
